- [x] 我读完了 issue 模板中的所有注释，确保填写符合要求。

- [x] 我搜索了 issues, 没有发现已提出的类似问题。
- [x] 问题在 Release 最新的版本上可以成功复现

### 描述

这个问题比较严重，很多Claude用户被封可能和这个issue有关

使用vless enc+xhttp+vision过Cloudflare ECH alpn=h3节点（用<https://github.com/Anthrop44/3x-setup>一键部署的），客户端为Linux v2rayN，使用Xray TUN和域名分流。在访问 openai.com 时被阻止访问并提示`Country, region, or territory not supported`而且被显示真实ip了。于是意识到有部分流量没有经过代理出口。切换到同一代理服务器的直连节点vless+xhttp+tls后访问恢复

实验确认这是因为UDP在Vision拒绝后通过客户端direct出站发送

确认该问题与ipv6无关

<details>
<summary>GPT分析的</summary>
### 原始部署与最小复现的关系

已通过只读SSH读取生产服务器正在使用的`/usr/local/x-ui/bin/config.json`和`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`，并核对服务端版本。没有修改或重启生产服务

| 生产节点 | VLESS Encryption | flow | 公网传输 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Direct h2/h3 | `encryption/decryption=none` | 无Vision | XHTTP + TLS，h2或h3 |
| Cloudflare ECH h2/h3 | `mlkem768x25519plus.xorpub`，客户端`0rtt`，服务端`600s` | `xtls-rprx-vision` | XHTTP + TLS/ECH，h2或h3 |

生产架构：

```text
Direct客户端 -> Caddy:443 -> h2c -> Xray Direct入站:8084
CDN客户端 -> Cloudflare边缘:443 -> Caddy回源监听 -> h2c -> Xray ENC+Vision入站:8087
```

所以从Cloudflare ECH h3切换到Direct h2同时改变了CDN路径、VLESS Encryption、Vision和ALPN，不能把恢复简单归因于h3变成h2。生产Xray的两个XHTTP入站均为`security=none`，TLS由Caddy/Cloudflare处理；这不代表公网传输没有TLS

最初曾用普通VLESS（`encryption=none`）+ RAW + TLS + Vision做本机最小复现，成功观察到同样的后续包direct现象。为了覆盖实际使用的VLESS ENC方案，本报告已追加并以**VLESS Encryption + XHTTP + TLS + Vision、ALPN h3**作为主要本机复现，且完成h2及flow对照

### 受控对照结果

下面各组使用相同的本机VLESS ENC密钥对、测试UUID、XHTTP路径、域名分流和默认direct规则。服务端仅监听回环地址，不经过Cloudflare或Caddy。每组发起两次相同curl HTTP/3请求，分别控制节点传输ALPN及客户端/服务端flow

注意两个不同层次：表中h2/h3是**客户端Xray到代理服务器的外层XHTTP传输**；测试应用curl始终使用HTTP/3，即内层UDP/443

| 外层ALPN | 客户端flow | Vision拒绝次数 | 客户端proxy记录 | 客户端direct记录 | UDP接收器收到包数 | 路径判断 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| h2 | `xtls-rprx-vision` | 4 | 4 | 2 | 2 | 拒绝后由客户端直连 |
| h3 | `xtls-rprx-vision` | 4 | 4 | 2 | 2 | 拒绝后由客户端直连 |
| h2 | `空（服务端同步不启用Vision）` | 0 | 2 | 0 | 10 | 客户端保持proxy，服务端转发 |
| h3 | `空（服务端同步不启用Vision）` | 0 | 2 | 0 | 10 | 客户端保持proxy，服务端转发 |
| h2 | `xtls-rprx-vision-udp443` | 0 | 2 | 0 | 10 | 客户端保持proxy，服务端转发 |
| h3 | `xtls-rprx-vision-udp443` | 0 | 2 | 0 | 10 | 客户端保持proxy，服务端转发 |

接收器和代理服务器都在同一台机器，所以“收到UDP包”本身不等于泄漏。路径判断同时核对客户端路由日志和服务端转发日志：普通Vision组的包由客户端direct发出；空flow及`-udp443`组的包由代理服务器转发，客户端没有direct记录。接收器不提供HTTP/3服务，所以各组curl最终都超时，不能以curl超时与否判断路径

实验说明：

- VLESS ENC+Vision在外层h2、h3下均复现，不是h3特有问题
- 普通VLESS+TLS+Vision也复现，所以VLESS Encryption不是必要条件
- 完全移除Cloudflare/ECH后仍复现，所以不能把问题限定为Cloudflare CDN或ECH故障
- 仅保留ENC、去掉Vision后，h2/h3两组没有出现该拒绝及后续direct路径
- 使用`xtls-rprx-vision-udp443`时，h2/h3两组均未出现本次泄漏路径；客户端写带后缀的flow，服务端仍写`xtls-rprx-vision`。这只是针对当前复现的对照结论，不声称该选项能消除所有域名嗅探失败/默认直连风险

### 实际与期望行为

主要h3复现的客户端源端口37731先命中proxy，被Vision拒绝后，同一源端口又命中direct；第二次请求的源端口33403重复此过程。本机UDP接收器收到两个1200字节数据包，客户端日志同时记录到相应direct连接

预期不是让普通Vision接受UDP/443，而是让已按域名判定需要代理、随后被Vision拒绝的UDP流，其后续包不会因为连接状态清理、重新嗅探不到域名而转为默认直连

版本与环境：

- 客户端和实际生产服务端均为Xray 26.10.31，commit `a4a3dff5b20c2faae567b742c172c7b95e75c083`，go1.27.3 linux/amd64
- 本机复现的服务端、客户端也使用同一个该版本二进制
- curl 8.18.0，OpenSSL 3.5.9，ngtcp2 1.22.1，nghttp3 1.18.0，支持HTTP3
- 完全本机复现不依赖v2rayN、TUN、真实代理节点、IPv6或外部网站

issues.body:
### Integrity requirements

- [X] I have read all the comments in the issue template and ensured that this issue meet the requirements.
- [X] I confirm that I have read the documentation, understand the meaning of all the configuration items I wrote, and did not pile up seemingly useful options or default values.
- [X] I provided the complete config and logs, rather than just providing the truncated parts based on my own judgment.
- [X] I searched issues and did not find any similar issues.
- [X] The problem can be successfully reproduced in the latest Release

### Description

> 简述：在 v26.10.17（与 main 相同）中，如果 XDRIVE 客户端在下载中途消失（进程被杀或断网），服务端无法察觉：它会继续从目标读取，并把剩余的整个响应写入存储（复现中 20 秒内写入约 235 MiB、607 个对象）。这些对象要等服务端的 mux 子连接自行结束后才会被清理（约 2.7–13 分钟），期间该会话仍被持续 LIST 轮询。原因是 XDRIVE 既没有对端存活检测，也没有背压。

Version: v26.10.17 (`92ccc93`, the newest release and the same commit as current `main`), `network: "xdrive"`, `service: "local"`. XDRIVE is only in the pre-releases since v26.9.30; it is not in v26.3.27. The session logic involved does not depend on the backend, so remote backends behave the same way.

When an XDRIVE client disappears in the middle of a download (process killed, network lost, which is common for mobile clients), the server does not notice:

1. It keeps reading from the target and writes the whole remaining response into the storage. In the repro the client had received 22 MiB of a 256 MiB body; within 20 s after the client was killed the server wrote 246,869,084 bytes in 607 objects.
2. These objects stay until the server-side mux sub-connection ends on its own: about 2.7 min when the target closes the connection after the body, about 13 min with a keep-alive target. Meanwhile the dead session is still polled (about 2 LIST per second).
3. The server logs nothing after the client is gone, even at `debug`.

With a remote backend every abandoned download can upload hundreds of MiB into the storage account, consume API quota and leave the objects there for minutes.

If only the application connection is closed while the client stays alive (curl killed), the server stops writing within about 5 s and the folder is cleaned up, so the problem is specific to the peer disappearing.

| 256 MiB body at 16 MiB/s, `sessionTtlSeconds: 30` | storage at +30 s | +90 s | +180 s | server kept writing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| download completes (control) | 0 B | 0 B | 0 B | no |
| client `kill -9` after ~2 s | 246,869,084 B / 607 objects | same | same | yes, the whole remaining body |
| client `SIGTERM` after ~2 s | 246,394,446 B / 515 objects | same | same | yes |
| curl killed, client alive | 0 B (one `.end`) | 0 B | 0 B | no, stopped within ~5 s |
| client `kill -9`, keep-alive target, watched 900 s | 246,453,796 B | same | same | yes; empty only at ~750–780 s |
| client `kill -9`, target sends `Connection: close` | 246,485,923 B | same | 0 B | yes; empty at ~165 s |

**Cause**

- `Listener.claim` marks the session active (`transport/internet/xdrive/xdrive.go:225`); the mark is removed only in the connection's `onClose` (`xdrive.go:234`). `collect()` skips active sessions (`xdrive.go:267-269`), so the folder of a dead session is not collected while the server-side connection is open.
- That connection is closed only when the inbound handler returns (`app/proxyman/inbound/worker.go:123-127`), i.e. after the server-side mux session ends. XDRIVE has no peer liveness signal: no heartbeat, no idle timeout. `Conn.receive` blocks on the reader channel (`conn.go:53-61`), `walReader.poll` returns quietly on an empty listing (`wal.go:295-297`), `holeTimeout` fires only when later segments exist (`wal.go:312-321`), EOF comes only from a `.end` object (`wal.go:365`).
- No backpressure: `walWriter.Write` appends to the buffer and `flushLocked` starts `go w.upload` (`wal.go:73-91`, `wal.go:127-156`); the semaphore in `upload` limits concurrent `Put`s, not unconsumed data (`wal.go:161-166`). Segments are deleted only by the peer's reader, so nothing limits what

issues.title: XHTTP: packet-down in stream-down with downlink keep-alive
issues.body:
# XHTTP: packet-down in stream-down with downlink keep-alive

Follows RPRX's packet-down design in https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/6755#issuecomment-5720463978, which was written while closing the earlier downlink-resume attempt (#6755). That attempt was rejected because "restore connection" is too complex, with latency, ACK and so on. This one does not attempt connection restoration at all. No reconnection, no state machine, nothing to tune: each stream-down GET stays a single request; if the GET dies, the connection dies the ordinary way.

## Problem (from #4846)

CDNs kill a stream-down GET on body inactivity. This matters during uploads: with packet-up the uplink posts keep flowing, but the downlink proxy payload only arrives while the origin sends, so during a pure upload the GET idles and gets cut. Same story for any target that goes quiet for a while after responding.

## What this PR adds

When enabled on both ends, the stream-down response body is cut into packet-down frames with the five elements from the design comment:

- omittable session id excerpt: first 8 bytes of the session id, present on data and keep-alive frames (absent in stream-one where the session id is empty)
- omittable packet seq: uint64, counting data/keep-alive frames per stream-down GET
- mandatory type: data or padding
- mandatory length: uint16
- payload

Use today is the first one from the design comment: downlink keep-alive. While the downlink has been idle for a whole period, the server writes a padding frame (base62, in the spirit of tokenish x-padding) instead of staying silent. Everything the dispatcher sends rides in data frames, which is what lets the client tell padding apart from payload safely; the seq keeps the format ready for the future uses listed in the design comment (retransmission, multi-path-down) without another wire change.

h1, h2 and h3 are covered, since the framers sit on the body, not on a specific transport. stream-one gets the same treatment on its single response body. Browser dialer is out of scope for now: it has no place to read the response header that confirms the framing.

## Negotiation

Strictly opt-in and per request, so old servers are unaffected and nothing breaks behind middleboxes:

1. client config has packetDown: XHTTP stream requests not used as pure uplink (stream-down GET, stream-one request) carry X-Packet-Down: 1
2. server has packetDown configured and sees the marker: it answers with X-Packet-Down: 1 on the response, and frames; without the confirmed header the client never parses frames
3. any other combination: byte-identical wire format as today

## Config

```jsonc
"xhttpSettings": {
  "path": "/sh",
  "packetDown": {              // absent = disabled, as today
    "keepAlive": true,
    "keepAlivePeriod": "10-30",  // seconds; padded when inactive this long. defaults to 10-30
    "keepAliveLength": "24-64"   // padding size. defaults to 24-64
  }
}
```

Server side is the same block in the inbound; the server only honors the feature when the client asks.

## Not in this PR (deliberately)

- obfs of the frames (later, per the design comment)
- retransmission, multi-path-down, same-packet racing, ACK: the format carries seq and the session excerpt, but none of the machinery, exactly like packet-up carries seq today without using it
- nothing about #4846's larger downlink freeze problem (the 15-20 KB per TCP connection cut): this only discards the CDN idle timer, it does not split data across connections

## Tests

- packet_down_test.go: frame round trip (with/without excerpt, with/without seq), byte-stream shaped like a socket, splitting payloads larger than one frame, padding skipped, malformed frame rejected, keep-alive written when idle, keep-alive suppressed while active, config normalization
- splithttp_test.go: full listen/dial round trip with packet-down on both end (100 KiB), and the fallback case with the client setting present but the server without one
- infra/conf: JSON un

issues.title: XHTTP client: Send only http/1.1 ALPN with uTLS fingerprint when using HTTP/1.1
issues.body:
## Problem

XHTTP client with TLS, `"alpn": ["http/1.1"]` and any uTLS `fingerprint` (including the default, since an empty fingerprint now means `chrome`) never works:

```
transport/internet/splithttp: failed to GET https://example.com/path/ > Get "...": net/http: HTTP/1.x transport connection broken: malformed HTTP response "\x00\x00\x12\x04\x00\x00..."
```

`decideHTTPVersion()` picks HTTP/1.1 from the configured ALPN, but the dialer calls `UConn.HandshakeContext()`, so the ClientHello carries the fingerprint's own ALPN. A packet capture shows `h2, http/1.1` in the ClientHello although the config only has `http/1.1`. Any h2-capable server (nginx with `http2 on`, Cloudflare) then negotiates h2 and answers with a SETTINGS frame, which Go's HTTP/1.1 transport cannot parse.

WS, HTTPUpgrade and RAW already handle this case with `WebsocketHandshakeContext()`, which rewrites the uTLS ALPN extension to `http/1.1` (and keeps the existing ECH behavior).

## Fix

Use `WebsocketHandshakeContext()` in the XHTTP dialer when the HTTP version is 1.1. Other HTTP versions are unchanged.

## Testing

Client: XHTTP + TLS, mode `auto` (resolves to `packet-up` for HTTP/1.1). Server: nginx (`http2 on`, `grpc_pass` to the XHTTP inbound), both direct and behind Cloudflare.

| alpn | fingerprint | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http/1.1` | chrome | fails, malformed HTTP response | works |
| `http/1.1` | firefox | fails, malformed HTTP response | works |
| `h2` | chrome / firefox | works | works |

`go test ./transport/internet/splithttp/ ./transport/internet/tls/` passes.

issues.title: VMess outbound ends the request when the client sends nothing for 100 ms (`TimeoutWrapperReader` returns no error on timeout)
issues.body:
### What happens

With an inbound that dispatches through `DispatchLink`, such as SOCKS, and a VMess outbound, a TCP connection whose
client sends nothing in its first 100 ms (about 300 ms with sniffing on) has its request ended for it. The VMess server reads the end of the request body, data the client sends afterwards never reaches the destination, and the connection is closed 1 to 2 s after the destination's last data (the server's `downlinkOnly` timeout).

Protocols where the server speaks first break: an SSH client that waits for the server's banner, SMTP, IMAP and POP3 without implicit TLS, FTP, MySQL. Clients that speak first (HTTP, TLS) are not affected.

### Cause

`TimeoutWrapperReader.ReadMultiBufferTimeout` in `common/buf/io.go` returns `nil, nil` when its wait runs out, where`pipe.Reader` returns `buf.ErrReadTimeout`, as the interface it implements says:

```go
// TimeoutReader is a reader that returns error if Read() operation takes longer than the given timeout.
```
```go
	case <-timeout:
		return nil, nil
```

`WrapLink` puts the reader of every link passed to `DispatchLink` behind this wrapper. The VMess outbound's first-payload step then gets no error:

```go
if err := buf.CopyOnceTimeout(input, bodyWriter, time.Millisecond*100); err != nil && err != buf.ErrNotTimeoutReader && err != buf.ErrReadTimeout {
```

so `CopyOnceTimeout` passes the empty `MultiBuffer` to `bodyWriter.WriteMultiBuffer`, and
`AuthenticationWriter.WriteMultiBuffer` (`common/crypto/auth.go`) seals an empty buffer as an empty chunk: the VMess server takes it as the end of the request body. With sniffing on, the sniffer's 200 ms wait comes first, then the outbound's 100 ms.

### Reproduction

1. Server: a VMess inbound over TCP, a `freedom` outbound, no `policy`.
2. Client: a SOCKS inbound on `127.0.0.1:10808` (sniffing on or off) and a VMess outbound to the server.
3. Through the SOCKS port, connect to an SSH server and send the client's line half a second in, as a client that waits for the banner does, keeping the connection open:
   `(sleep 0.5; printf 'SSH-2.0-test\r\n'; sleep 10) | nc -X 5 -x 127.0.0.1:10808 <ssh-server> 22`

Expected: after the banner, the SSH server answers with its key exchange, and the connection stays open until the server or `nc` closes it.

Actual: the banner arrives, nothing comes back for the line, and the connection is closed 1 to 2 s after the banner.
Sending nothing ends the same way. Without the `sleep 0.5`, the server answers and the connection stays open.

### Fix

```diff
--- a/common/buf/io.go
+++ b/common/buf/io.go
@@ -73,7 +73,7 @@
 		}
 		return r.mb, r.err
 	case <-timeout:
-		return nil, nil
+		return nil, ErrReadTimeout
 	}
 }
```

This is `pipe.Reader`'s behaviour, and every caller already handles it: `CopyOnceTimeout` in the VMess, Trojan and Shadowsocks outbounds and in mux, the VLESS outbound's first-payload read, and the dispatcher's sniffer, which then stops at its first timed-out wait, after the same 200 ms. With the change, the reproduction above works: the late line reaches the server, which answers, and the connection stays open.

### Versions

Since v25.8.29: the wrapper came with the move of the SOCKS, HTTP and Tunnel inbounds to `DispatchLink` (`56a45ad578`), and returns `nil, nil` on timeout from its first version. Still on `main` at `7c8dbcb4bb`. Seen with a build of commit
`52a412d9e2f5`.

### Related

#7233 met the same `nil, nil` from the sniffer's side, treated an empty read as a valid result and changed only the sniffer (closed, not merged). VMess cannot take it that way: its empty write ends the request. #7238 fixed another place where a reader passed to `DispatchLink` behaves unlike a pipe.

issues.title: common/buf/io.go: TimeoutWrapperReader returns ErrReadTimeout when timeout
issues.body:
Fixes #7318.

When `TimeoutWrapperReader` reaches its deadline, returning `(nil, nil)` makes `CopyOnceTimeout` treat the timeout as a successful empty read and write an empty request body. For VMess, that seals the request before a server-first client sends payload.

Return `ErrReadTimeout` to preserve the timeout contract. The current VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks, and mux callers already handle this error as an expected timeout.

Checks: not run (no target-required check was specified for this one-line correction).

issues.title: TUN inbound: Ignore `dns` IPv6 setup error when neither `gateway` nor `autoSystemRoutingTable` has an IPv6 entry on Windows
issues.body:
### Problem Description
On Windows 11 24H2 (OS Build 26100+), starting Xray in native TUN mode fails with:
```
proxy/tun: xray_tun up: failed to set dns: Access is denied.
```

### Root Cause Analysis
1. In Windows 11 24H2, the NSI/TCP stack allocates an MIB row for IPv6 on newly created Wintun virtual adapters even if IPv6 is systemically disabled or has `DisabledComponents = 0x28`.
2. As a result, `t.luid.IPInterface(windows.AF_INET6)` returns `nil` instead of `windows.ERROR_NOT_FOUND`.
3. Execution then reaches `t.luid.SetDNS(windows.AF_INET6, dns, nil)`, which invokes `SetInterfaceDnsSettings` with `DNS_INTERFACE_SETTINGS_VERSION1` and `DNS_SETTING_IPV6`.
4. Windows kernel rejects this call with Win32 Error 5 (`ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED`) because the Wintun interface possesses no unicast IPv6 address (`unicastAddresses` is empty).

### Changes in this PR
1. **Guard Loop by Configured State**: Check whether the address or route is actually configured for the protocol family. If neither `address` nor `route` is present, safely skip `IPInterface` and `SetDNS`.
2. **SetDNS Guard by Unicast Address**: Skip `SetDNS()` on families without assigned unicast IP addresses, which prevents Win32 Error 5.
3. **Preserve Empty DNS Clearing Semantics**: Distribute configured DNS servers into `familyDNS`. If an addressed family is provided with an empty DNS list, it still passes the empty slice to `SetDNS()` to clear existing DNS servers, maintaining proper DNS lifecycle semantics.

### Test Verification
Tested on Windows 11 24H2 (Build 26100.2161) with Wintun 0.14.1 across 6 scenarios:
- [x] **IPv4-only TUN**: Successfully creates and configures the adapter without `Access is denied`.
- [x] **Dual-stack IPv4 + IPv6**: Correctly applies routes and DNS to both families.
- [x] **IPv4 DNS + IPv6 Route (`::/0`)**: Sets IPv4 DNS while skipping IPv6 `SetDNS` on unaddressed IPv6 interface.
- [x] **Empty DNS clearing**: Correctly passes empty slice to addressed interfaces to reset DNS.
- [x] **Process SIGKILL & rapid restart**: Rapid recovery on existing adapter name without registry corruption.
- [x] **External IPv6 leak prevention**: WFP block leak rules verified 100% effective.

issues.title: VLESS protocol: Add lightweight, Post-Quantum ML-KEM-768-based PFS 1-RTT / anti-replay 0-RTT AEAD Encryption
issues.body:
~~经 @gfw-killer 一人 [多次](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4952#issuecomment-3129991254) [血书](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4915#issuecomment-3102172861)，VLESS 自带加密它终于来了！~~

我想把这个 spec 写得言简意赅，想要了解更多设计过程中的取舍，请参考 https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4952#issuecomment-3159885555 开始的相关讨论，以及 https://t.me/projectXtls/1005 开始的 Q/A 碎片，非常感谢 @Fangliding @wwqgtxx @ForestL18 @xchacha20-poly1305 等人参与讨论、反馈

## VLESS Encryption 设计理念与通信流程

就像一年前说过的那样，鉴于 GFW 已经将全随机数外观列入黑名单，**VLESS 加密原生外观并非全随机数**（头部有公钥特征，流量为 TLSv1.3 的 `23 3 3 l>>8 l` AEAD 头特征，**但可选 XOR 以变成全随机数外观**），重点是有 SS 2022/AEAD、VMess 等协议都没有的 **更高的安全性（前向安全且抗量子），以及更好的性能（且建议开 XTLS 避免二次加解密），并且同样是 0-RTT，以确保它可以成为更好的替代品，适用于 CDN（避免暴露 UUID 及被代理的 SNI）、中转（禁 HTTP/TLS）、non-TLS（伊朗 HTTP）等场景**

特别注意这个加密不是让你直接过墙用的，类似的协议早已不适合直接过墙，直接过墙应使用 [REALITY](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4915)、[XHTTP](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/discussions/4113)、[Vision](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/discussions/1295) 等协议

~~REALITY 则不需要再加密 VLESS，但如果你用机场，你也可以把机场线路当中转，转到你的免费 VPS，从而绕过机场的审计~~

就像五年前 VLESS BETA 里提到的加密设计理念与当时预留的配置结构一样，**VLESS 加密的设计是在明文 VLESS 协议外加一层 conn，而不与内层 VLESS 协议耦合，易于实现、易于替换，并且最大字节限制为 8K/16K，避免了额外 copy，从而不损失性能**

我写了两版加密，最终留下的是第二版，它非常简洁，实现细节请看代码，这里简单说一下通信流程：

0. 无论是 1-RTT 还是 0-RTT，客户端每次发起连接后都发送基于配置中多个公钥的 ivAndRelays，以实现解密前的多次中转
1. C client hello：nfsKey 加密的长度、nfsKey 加密的前向安全 MLKEM768X25519 公钥、nfsKey 加密的 padding
2. S server hello：nfsKey 加密的前向安全 MLKEM768X25519 公钥、unitedKey 加密的 ticket、unitedKey 加密的 padding
3. C ticket hello：nfsKey 加密的长度、nfsKey 加密的 ticket、unitedKey 加密的内层 VLESS 协议
4. S random hello：16 字节随机数、unitedKey 加密的内层 VLESS 协议（unitedKey 均为协商出的 pfsKey 加 nfsKey）
5. **以后的连接可以直接从 3 开始而无需 1-RTT 密钥协商，从而实现了 0-RTT，ticket 复用时间由服务端设置，建议十分钟**
6. 服务端将每次的 nfsKey 存入 map 以防重放，十分钟后全扔；若收到了不认识的 ticket，回复无意义随机数流

若选择了 "xorpub"，客户端会对 ivAndRelays 中的公钥进行 XOR 以消除 X25519 public key 和 ML-KEM-768 ciphertext 的特征
若选择了 "random"，客户端、服务端还会对 `23 3 3 l>>8 l` 进行 XOR 以实现全随机数外观，**占整体流量的万分之六，成本极低**

- 为了避免固定的流量长度特征，**客户端、服务端必须将 ivAndRelays、client/server hello 与 padding/data 粘包 write**
- 为了预留把连接交给内层 VLESS flow 前模拟出任何流量长度特征的可能性，**客户端不能等收完服务端 padding 再进行下一步**
- **Data 的 header 与 TLSv1.3 相同，是为了在可选 XTLS 裸奔时让观察者难以区分何时开始裸奔**
- 更多考虑请参考代码中的详细注释，MPL 或 GPL 的 Go 程序直接复制过去就能用，**比如 Mihomo v1.19.13 已支持**

关于“解密前的多次中转”，是因为我看 SS 系列很喜欢搞 relay 这种东西，~~说实话我也不太清楚应用场景甚至还在频道调研了一下，最终还是给 VLESS Encryption 加上了，毕竟也就是加个 for 的事~~，不同的是每一级都基于公私钥机制，且有对下一级 relay 的关联机制以使其不可被替换，~~因为我比较喜欢开脑洞去想如何攻击代理协议，就像代码中有多处注释说明了关于避免“[移花接木](https://github.com/shadowsocks/shadowsocks-org/issues/183)”等攻击的考虑~~，服务端那个 for 其实就一次，因为到服务端只剩最后一级了，所以接下来还会出一个 vless-relay/core 项目~~以方便滥用中转~~

## VLESS Encryption 对比 SS、VMess

### 客户端配置安全、前向安全、0-RTT

~~我最后悔的事情就是两年前没有放出 REALITY 的文章~~，使得 REALITY 加密/认证/伪装的设计取舍没有清晰地呈现出来，**尤其是至今一众小白仍傻傻分不清不同协议的加密/认证安全等级，以为加了密就是一样的**，这次正好把概念给大家讲清楚，不重蹈覆辙。

**客户端配置安全：若攻击者拿到了客户端配置，无法解密以前、以后的通信内容，无法对以后的通信进行 MITM（中间人攻击）。** 这个安全概念没有前向安全那么常见，~~不知道是不是代理领域独一份~~，但它非常重要，**因为通过读取剪切板、输入法上传、通讯软件分享、国产反诈手机等方式想拿到你的客户端配置可以说是没有难度。**

**前向安全：若攻击者拿到了长期密钥（一般指服务端的），无法解密以前的通信内容。一般来说对以后的通信内容也无法直接解密，而是只能 MITM。** 实现前向安全一般基于 TLS/REALITY ECDHE 或抗量子的“双方临时密钥交换”，但是会增加 1-RTT。

**比如 SS 2022/AEAD（以及基于它们的 ShadowTLS）、VMess 采用对称 PSK 的设计，并没有实现客户端配置安全、前向安全，都是看似加密但实际上没有任何保障，GFW 拿到了你手机上的配置后，甚至还能直接解密你电脑等其它设备的流量（~~即使只是 SNI 也方便了监控~~）。** 还有一些协议是拿到客户端配置即可 MITM，~~只能说是一言难尽~~。

~~并且随着 X25519 受到未来量子计算机的威胁与日俱增，也不只是 SNI 了，人家确实可以现在记录、未来破解你 SS 中的一些 TLS。~~

确实不止是 SNI 了，GFW 现在就可以对内层 TLS 进行 MITM 从而甚至解密被代理的 TLS，问题很大：https://github.com/net4people/bbs/issues/526

**VLESS Encryption 类似于 REALITY，每一级 relay 都通过预共享 ML-KEM-768/X25519 密钥对的方式实现了客户端配置安全，并且通过双方临时 MLKEM768X25519 密钥交换的方式实现了前向安全。** 密钥交换过程也是加密的，其实比 REALITY/TLS 更安全，比如说后者可能会因为明文 X25519 被未来的量子计算机破解而被解密流量，但对于 VLESS Encryption 则必须先拿到服务端私钥。

然而“双方临时密钥交换”会增加 1-RTT，这是用户不愿意看到的，**所以 VLESS Encryption 通过跨连接复用 pfsKey 的方式实现了首次密钥交换后的 0-RTT**。可能有人会说你都跨连接复用 pfsKey 了还“前向安全”吗，1-RTT 加多路复用岂不是更符合定义？然而多路复用若 pfsKey+nfsKey 泄露了同样是能解密出所有被代理的连接，**多路复用十分钟与跨连接复用 pfsKey 十分钟是等价的，甚至我每个 0-RTT 连接实际加密都是不同的 unitedKey，安全性更高**。无论哪种方式，实践中十分钟复用级别的前向安全已经足够，如果你把

issues.title: sockopt.interface: when the interface does not exist, the dial silently goes unbound (can loop back into TUN)
issues.body:
### Integrity requirements

- [x] I have read all the comments in the issue template and ensured that this issue meet the requirements.
- [x] I confirm that I have read the documentation, understand the meaning of all the configuration items I wrote, and did not pile up seemingly useful options or default values.
- [x] I provided the complete config and logs, rather than just providing the truncated parts based on my own judgment.
- [x] I searched issues and did not find any similar issues.
- [x] The problem can be successfully reproduced in the latest Release

### Description

If an outbound has `streamSettings.sockopt.interface` set and that interface does not exist at dial time, Xray does not fail the dial. It logs `failed to apply socket options > failed to get interface ...` at **Info** level and opens the connection without any binding, so it follows the system routing table.

`transport/internet/system_dialer.go` (v26.10.10, lines 134-139; same in v26.9.9) only logs the error returned by `applyOutboundSocketOptions` and goes on to `dialer.DialContext`. The UDP path does the same (lines 77-81). The error itself comes from `net.InterfaceByName` in `transport/internet/sockopt_darwin.go:136-140`. From reading the source, Linux takes the same path (the error is logged, not returned); I tested macOS only.

Why this matters. A typical full-tunnel setup on a desktop routes everything into a TUN interface handled by Xray (default route split as 0.0.0.0/1 + 128.0.0.0/1 into the TUN), and binds outbounds with `sockopt.interface` so that their own sockets do not enter the TUN again. If the bound interface goes away, the fallback sends the outbound's sockets into the TUN, Xray routes them to the same outbound, and the connection loops.

We hit this loop in practice on macOS. A separate OpenVPN client provided a corporate network through its own utun interface, and the corporate subnet was routed to a freedom outbound so that it would follow that VPN's route. At night the OpenVPN client lost its connection and its utun interface was removed. From then on, every connection to the corporate subnet (including DNS queries to the corporate DNS server) entered the TUN, came back to the same outbound and entered the TUN again. When we looked, there were about 8,000 looped connections, all 16,384 ephemeral ports were in use, and other processes on the host got `EADDRNOTAVAIL` (`Can't assign requested address`) on connect until the loop was broken by restarting Xray.

In that incident the outbound had no `sockopt.interface` at all, so the loop itself is a config problem. The obvious fix is to bind the outbound to the other VPN's interface (`"interface": "utunN"`), so that it can never fall into the TUN. That does not work because of this issue: once the interface disappears, the binding is skipped and the loop is back. The only visible sign is an Info-level log line, which is hidden at the usual `warning` level.

Expected: if the interface named in `sockopt.interface` cannot be found, the dial fails (fail closed), as a bound socket does when its interface has no route. At the very least the error should be logged as a warning. A silent fallback to the routing table defeats the purpose of binding: it can send traffic into a tunnel (loop) or past it (leak).

### Reproduction Method

No server and no TUN are needed. Run Xray with the config below (interface `utun99` does not exist) and send a request through the SOCKS inbound:

```

issues.title: Feature Request: Add udp+local:// DNS scheme (plain UDP local mode)
issues.body:
# Feature Request: Add `udp+local://` DNS scheme (plain UDP local mode)

## Summary

Xray's DNS configuration supports `+local` variants for HTTPS, h2c, QUIC and TCP, but there is **no `udp+local` scheme** for plain UDP DNS in local mode. This means there is currently **no way to send plain UDP DNS queries to a local resolver while bypassing the routing/dispatcher stack**.

## Current state

`app/dns/nameserver.go`, `NewServer()` switch (main branch):

```go
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https"):      // DoH remote
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "h2c"):        // DoH h2c remote
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "https+local"): // DoH local
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "h2c+local"):   // DoH h2c local
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "quic+local"):  // DoQ local
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "tcp"):         // TCP remote
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "tcp+local"):   // TCP local
case strings.EqualFold(u.String(), "fakedns"):
```

Every protocol except plain UDP has a `+local` form. Plain UDP falls through to the default branch:

```go
if dest.Network == net.Network_UDP {
    return NewClassicNameServer(dest, dispatcher, ...)
}
```

Note that `NewClassicNameServer` receives the `dispatcher`, so plain UDP **always goes through the routing stack** — there is no way to bypass it.

## Why this matters (measured data)

For a local resolver (e.g. smartdns on `127.0.0.1`), bypassing the dispatcher matters. Measured on a local resolver over loopback, one A + one AAAA query for the same domain:

| Path | p50 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `tcp+local://` (current workaround) | ~810µs | 2 TCP handshakes + 2 closes |
| `tcp+local://` pipelined on 1 conn | ~680µs | would need connection pooling, not implemented |
| **plain UDP, 2 packets sent in parallel** | **~376µs** | no handshake, no teardown |

The UDP path is ~2x faster than the current `tcp+local` workaround because it avoids TCP handshake/teardown entirely. Pairing responses by DNS ID worked in 200/200 trials with zero mismatch.

For users running a local caching resolver, this overhead is paid on every cache-miss lookup.

## Secondary issue: port parsing for bare `udp://` schemes

Related bug found while investigating. With:

```json
"dns": { "servers": ["udp://127.0.0.1:5353"] }
```

xray logs:

```
DNS: created UDP client initialized for udp://127.0.0.1:5353:53
```

The port becomes `5353:53` — the `:5353` is swallowed into the address (as a domain string) and then a default `:53` is appended by:

```go
// app/dns/nameserver_udp.go:41
if address.Port == 0 {
    address.Port = net.Port(53)
}
```

This is because `infra/conf/dns.go` builds the endpoint with `Address` and `Port` as separate fields, and `Address.Build()` calls `net.ParseAddress()` on the whole string including `:5353`, while `Port` stays 0.

Attempting `udp://127.0.0.1` (no port) resolves to `udp://127.0.0.1:53`, which happens to work, but the scheme is still parsed as a domain so the connection fails with:

```
failed to open connection to udp:udp://127.0.0.1:53
> too many colons in address
```

Contrast with `tcp+local`, which parses correctly because it uses `url.Hostname()` and `url.Port()` separately (`app/dns/nameserver_tcp.go:75-81`).

## Proposed change

Add a `udp+local` case that mirrors `tcp+local` — parse host/port via `url.Hostname()` / `url.Port()` and pass `nil` as the dispatcher:

```go
case strings.EqualFold(u.Scheme, "udp+local"): // DNS-over-UDP Local mode
    return NewUDPNameServer(u, nil, disableCache, serveStale, serveExpiredTTL, clientIP), nil
```

Where the new constructor resolves the destination the same way `baseTCPNameServer` does:

```go
port := net.Port(53)
if url.Port() != "" {
    if port, err = net.PortFromString(url.Port()); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
}
dest := net.UDPDestination(net.ParseAddress(url.Hostname()), port)
```

This would also give users a documented way to hit a local resolver on a non-53 port without the address-swallowing bug.

## Environment

issues.title: XHTTP server: unblock writes and serialize connection close
issues.body:
## Summary

An XHTTP response write can hold the connection mutex while blocked on a slow reader. Closing the logical connection then waits on that mutex, including when a proxy inactivity timeout cancels the business context while the HTTP request stays open.

Signal closure before waiting for the writer and interrupt an active write using `http.ResponseController`. Serialize the complete transition with `sync.Once` so concurrent business/handler closes join the deadline call and the writer before `ServeHTTP` returns.

```text
Close (once)
  signal closure
  interrupt active write
  wait for writer completion
```

## Evidence

- Added `TestConcurrentCloseWaitsForDeadline`, using a real HTTP test server and a gated response writer. The gates ensure the business close owns the first deadline call before the handler closes.
- Upstream implementation: fails with `Close waited for the blocked writer without interrupting it`.
- An unserialized close transition: fails with `deadline call outlived ServeHTTP during concurrent Close`.
- Commit `8628110`, rebuilt with Go 1.27.3 on Linux/amd64: `go test -buildvcs=false ./transport/internet/splithttp -count=1` passes (`ok`, 2.434s).
- Bounded loopback `packet-up` fixtures run against a binary rebuilt from commit `8628110`: peer half-close and an internal inactivity timeout with the HTTP request still open both finish with `CLOSE_FRAMES=0`, `WRITE_FRAMES=0`, and `CLOSE_WAIT_CONNECTIONS=0`.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way.

**Blast Radius:** XHTTP shutdown. Active I/O is interrupted on close; the existing transport tests cover normal completion.

issues.title: XHTTP: Add configurable response headers
issues.body:
## What

Adds an optional `responseHeaders` map (`map<string, string>`) to the XHTTP inbound settings, giving the server control over the headers it writes on responses.

Currently the hub hardcodes a set of response headers: the CORS block for the browser dialer (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`), `X-Accel-Buffering`, `Cache-Control` and the SSE `Content-Type`. With `responseHeaders` an operator can add, override, or remove any of them, as well as set arbitrary extra response headers.

## Semantics

- A key that doesn't collide with a default header is added to every response.
- A key that matches a hardcoded header overrides it.
- An empty value removes that header from the response entirely (including the hardcoded ones).
- When `responseHeaders` is unset, the behavior is byte-identical to before.

Example:

```json
"xhttpSettings": {
  "path": "/api/v2/stream",
  "responseHeaders": {
    "Server": "nginx",
    "Cache-Control": "no-cache, no-transform",
    "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "https://example.com",
    "X-Accel-Buffering": ""
  }
}
```

## Why

- The CORS headers only matter for the browser dialer; a plain server deployment currently emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every response, which is undesirable behind a specific origin and gets flagged by security reviews.
- Reverse-proxy and CDN setups sometimes require specific response headers (`Server`, `Via`, custom headers) or different cache semantics.
- Operators running behind intermediaries may want the response header set to stay consistent with the profile of the service they front, instead of carrying markers that no other service on that endpoint emits.

## Notes

- Server-side only; the client ignores it. It round-trips through `extra` like the other settings.
- `config.pb.go` regenerated with protoc v6.33.5 / protoc-gen-go v1.36.11 — the header matches all existing `.pb.go` files (`check-proto` passes; I verified the unmodified proto regenerates byte-identical with this toolchain first).

## Tests

- `Test_SetResponseHeader`: default / override / removal via empty value.
- `Test_WriteResponseHeader_ResponseHeaders`: CORS default, override, removal, custom header addition, origin echo.
- `go test ./...` passes locally across all packages, except the pre-existing network-dependent `TestQUICNameServer` in `app/dns`, which fails identically on pristine `main` in my environment (no QUIC egress).

issues.title: Inbound: Close and remove the handler when it fails to start
issues.body:
`inbound.Manager.AddHandler` first puts the handler into `taggedHandlers` (or `untaggedHandlers`) and, when the manager is already running, then calls `handler.Start()` and returns its error. Nothing is undone when `Start` fails.

This is the path of `HandlerService.AddInbound` (`xray api adi`). If the new inbound cannot start, for example because one of its ports is already in use, the API returns the error but the handler stays in the manager. Adding it again with the same tag fails with `existing tag found` until it is removed by hand, and the workers that did start (the ports before the busy one in a port range) keep listening.

Now a handler that fails to start is taken out of the manager again and closed, so the ports it opened are released and the tag can be used again. Startup is not affected: handlers from the config are only started later by `Manager.Start`.

Verified with the new `TestAddHandlerFailedStart`, which adds a tagged and an untagged handler whose `Start` fails to a running manager, and then adds the tag again. On main it fails with:

    handler "in" was not closed after failing to start
    handler "in" is still registered after failing to start (1 handlers)

With this change it passes. I also checked it end to end with a dokodemo-door inbound on two ports where the second one was busy: on main the first port stayed bound after the failed add, and adding the inbound again after freeing the port failed with `existing tag found: in`. With the change the first port is free again and the second add works.

Also ran `go test ./app/proxyman/inbound/...` (also with `-race`), `go test ./testing/scenarios -run TestCommander`, `go vet ./app/proxyman/inbound/...`, gofmt and `go run ./infra/vformat/main.go -mode check -pwd ./`.

issues.title: grpc: close cached clients with their outbound handler
issues.body:
Related to #7177. Requesting review of resource ownership, shutdown semantics, and API compatibility

## Problem

Outbound gRPC clients are cached by destination and MemoryStreamConfig, but core shutdown never closes or removes them. In an embedding process that stays alive, clients can retain connections and continue reconnecting after their core has stopped.

## Change

Give memory stream settings synchronous close-hook registration, and close the resources from their owning outbound handler. Register each ClientConn for exact-entry cache removal and ClientConn.Close. Refuse both reuse and creation after owner closure starts; racing creation must either register for cleanup or close its unpublished client. Cleanup runs outside the settings/cache locks, and concurrent Close callers wait for the same result.

The supported Instance lifecycle is single-start. Each fresh core retains separate ownership even when endpoint and outbound tags match. No per-run generation model, idle-timeout change or per-RPC closure of the shared ClientConn is added.

## Validation

- Synthetic regression reproduces the problem on v26.3.27 and main da2248c.
- `go test -race ./transport/internet ./transport/internet/grpc -count=1 -timeout=120s` passes on this exact branch.
- Official `go run ./infra/vformat/main.go -mode check -pwd ./` passes.
- Tests cover two live cores, sibling streams, normal/MultiMode, fresh-core cycles, failed-start cleanup, multiple destinations, owner/acquisition races, cancellation/backoff and forced dialerProxy lookup contention with Manager.Close.
- Earlier candidate testing also ran the target race suites five times and the dialerProxy test ten times. Those results are supplementary, not a claim that the whole upstream suite passes.

## Review questions / limits

- Handler.Close previously always returned nil. This candidate propagates cleanup errors. Is propagation preferred, or should transport cleanup be logged while preserving the existing return policy? Embedders must distinguish a cleanup error from a still-running core.
- MemoryStreamConfig with resource/mutex state must not be copied; direct external transport callers must close their settings.
- Manager.RemoveHandler still bypasses Handler.Close. XHTTP/nested download settings and TUN eventfd cleanup remain unfixed.
- No general multi-instance guarantee for Xray's other process-global networking state, TLS/Reality/masking matrix, or physical Android packet boundary is claimed.

This is intended as a draft for ownership/API review, not a claim that the Android product defect is resolved.

issues.title: Finalmask: Add the `lua` mask (noise's `script` moves there)
issues.body:
#7174 bolted a second Lua mask onto header-custom, which was the wrong way around. One `lua` mask covers all of it now: it is both a `tcpMasks` and a `udpMasks` entry, and the script decides what it does by the hooks it defines.

-- `HandleHeader(stream, address, role)`, TCP: a free handshake before any traffic, with `stream:Write`, `stream:Read` and `stream:Sleep`. Return a string or an error and the connection is dropped
-- `HandleHeaderWrite(header, address, role)` and `HandleHeaderRead(packet, address, role)`, UDP: prefix every packet with a header, and strip it on the other side by returning its length, or `nil` to drop the packet
-- `HandleNoise(plan, address, role)` is the old noise hook, so `noise`'s `script` is gone (it has not been in a release yet)
-- `role` is `client` or `server`, so one file serves both ends
-- a hook the script does not define is not wrapped at all: a noise only script leaves TCP connections alone and never touches a packet
-- the module is `xray.finalmask` now, with `Random` and `RandomBetween`

```json
{
    "udpMasks": [{"type": "lua", "settings": {"script": "mask.lua", "reset": "30-60"}}]
}
```

Per call it takes at most 64 noise packets and 65535 bytes of noise, 1024 bytes of header, and 65535 bytes each way in a handshake. A packet hook gets 1s, a handshake 30s. A UDP header is one Lua call per packet, the benchmarks in the package cover its cost.

The static lists can follow later, the same script can already do what they do.

issues.title: Outbound: Close the handler when removing it; VLESS Reverse Proxy: Don't start after closing
issues.body:
`outbound.Manager.RemoveHandler`, which `xray api rmo` (`HandlerService.RemoveOutbound`) calls, deletes the handler from the map but never closes it, while `inbound.Manager.RemoveHandler` does. So whatever the removed outbound's `Close()` would release keeps running:

- WireGuard creates its TUN in the constructor (a kernel TUN when available, otherwise a gVisor stack), and once used also has the device with its UDP socket and keepalives.
- VLESS with `reverse` keeps its monitor task: the removed outbound keeps dialing the server every 2 s.
- Same for MASQUE's tunnel. VLESS with `testpre` gets closed too, but its pre-connects only stop reliably with #7113: on main, `Close()` stops just the goroutines waiting to hand over a connection, not the ones redialing an unreachable server.

This shows up wherever outbounds are added and removed at runtime through the API, e.g. by panels.

### Changes

- `RemoveHandler` closes the handler it removed. It does so after releasing the manager lock, so a slow `Close()` (WireGuard) doesn't hold up `Select()`/`GetHandler()` for new connections. Removing an unknown tag still returns nil, and a removed handler is closed only once, since `Manager.Close()` no longer sees it.
- VLESS starts the reverse 2 s after the outbound is created (a goroutine in `New()`), so an outbound removed within those 2 s would still start it after `Close()`. `Reverse.Start()` is now a no-op once `Reverse.Close()` has run.

The other callers of `RemoveHandler` (commander, metrics, reverse portal, VLESS inbound's reverse) remove their own internal outbounds, whose `Close()` is a no-op or idempotent.

Connections already in flight on a removed outbound behave as before unless its `Close()` tears them down (WireGuard, MASQUE). A reverse bridge that is already connected is left to end on its own; only new ones stop.

### Reproduction (on 836a6fe)

Client: `api` with `HandlerService` behind a dokodemo-door inbound, `freedom` as the only configured outbound. Server: a plain TCP listener that only counts accepted connections.

**VLESS `reverse`**: the outbound is added with `xray api ado` and removed with `xray api rmo`. Afterwards `xray api lso` lists only the `freedom` outbound in all runs.

| `rmo` after `ado` | build | accepts at `rmo` | 3 s later | 13 s later |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 7 s | main | 3 | 4 | 9 |
| 7 s | this PR | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| 0.5 s | main | 0 | 1 | 6 |
| 0.5 s | this PR | 0 | 0 | 0 |

**WireGuard** (`noKernelTun: true`): five outbounds, each added with `ado` and removed right away with `rmo`. Goroutines from the `metrics` listener's `/debug/pprof/goroutine`: main 11 → 72, this PR 11 → 12.

issues.body:
```markdown
Follow-up to #6487, covering the startup-padding part of #6732.

Adds an optional `padding` array to XMC settings with configurable direction per turn:

```json
{
  "padding": [
    {"length": "44", "direction": "c2s"},
    {"length": "64-128", "direction": "s2c"},
    {"length": "25", "direction": "c2s"},
    {"length": "32768-49152", "direction": "s2c"}
  ]
}
```

Each entry specifies a fixed length or inclusive range, plus direction (`"c2s"` for client-to-server or `"s2c"` for server-to-client; full names `"client-to-server"` and `"server-to-client"` are also accepted). Turns can be in any order and direction, including consecutive same-direction turns. Both endpoints need the same array. issues.title: Bound shutdown after termination signal
issues.body:
This change prevents Xray from waiting indefinitely during graceful shutdown after receiving SIGTERM or interrupt.

Previously, shutdown depended on the deferred server.Close() call returning. If any feature Close() path blocked, the process could stay alive while listeners or active connections continued operating. This made stale Xray processes difficult to detect, especially when another process could bind the same port.

Now Xray runs server.Close() explicitly after receiving a termination signal and waits up to 10 seconds. If shutdown does not complete in time, the process exits with code 1 so supervisors can treat it as a failed shutdown and avoid leaving a functional stale process behind.

This issue was most visible on mobile clients. Some apps, such as Telegram proxy-style traffic, may continue using an already-established path even when the VPN/client UI appears disabled. If the old Xray process remains alive during a stuck shutdown, those connections can continue transferring traffic and updating usage counters, making the node look stopped from the client side while traffic is still flowing server-side.

issues.title: TLS : tls spoofing
issues.body:
fix #5964

### RawPacket aka TLS Spoofing

So first lets talk about the idea,

when you connect to a xray server, the censors can see your TLS ClientHello, read the SNI, and figure out what you are doing and block :)

The RawPacket aka TLS spoofing fixes that by injecting a fake TLS ClientHello before the real one Hits.


The fake one carries like a decoy domain (ex. baidu.com) and then the real one carries your actual destination (ex. www.example.com).

A sensor that captures the first packet sees baidu.com and think that you are just browsing, and everything is okay with that, but in reality your connection goes through :)


It can be configured in the `finalmask.tcp` okay? and its only for client side.


### How everything works


When Xray dials a TCP connection and the first `Write()` happens (which also triggers the real TLS handshake) , our Raw Packet setup does the following.

1.builds a fake Tls ClientHello with whatever SNI you want or you have option to provide the raw bytes (b64).

2.Then we. wrap it in a raw TCP/ip packet.

3.Then deliberately we corrupt the TCP header using whatever method is selected okay?

4. Then we shoot it out via a raw socket

5. Then immediately let the real `Write()` go through normally


In short : two packets arrive at the server back to back and the fake one gets dropped by the servers TCP stack because of the corruption and then the real handshake proceeds like nothing happened.


### Config Example

```json
{
  "streamSettings": {
    "finalmask": {
      "tcp": [
        {
          "type": "rawpacket",
          "settings": {
            "sni": "baidu.com",
            "payload": "",
            "method": "wrong-sequence",
            "ttl": 3,
            "count": 1
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```


### Available Fields

`sni` : The domain to put in the fake ClientHello. If you set this, it will auto generate a valid TLS ClientHello for you automatically. If you set `payload` and `sni` same time , sni wins here.

```
"sni": "baidu.com"
```

`payload` : If you don't want an auto gnrated ClientHello, then just encode your raw bytes that you want into base64 and put them here. I have added an option to do it from command line also. Do like this 

```
 xray tls fake-hello google.com
 ```

It will out the thing and then just copy paste.


Note : If `sni` and payload are empty or not set , the raw packet does nothing and the connection goes through normally.


`method` : It defines how we corrupt the fake packet so the server drops it.

`wrong-sequence` : It duplicates the sequence number (looks like a retransmission so server drops it)

So we grab the kernels `snd_nxt` ( the next sequence number the kernel expects to send), then subtract the length of the fake payload and then use that as the sequence number of the injected packet. The results then is a duplicate of the. last segment, so the receivers TCP stack sees it as a retransmit at best, or like out of window at worst and then drops it.


`wrong-checksum`: It flips all the bits in the TCP checksum (so server sees a bad checksum and drops it)

We build the packet with a correct checksum and then flip every bit(^0xFFFF). The receiver then validates the checksum and its wrong, so the packet goes in trash.

`wrong-ack`: It sets ACK number way outside the receive window (so server sends dup ACK then drops it)

It sets the ACK number to `rcv_nxt - window/2` and that's way outside of the receivers window, and the kernel responds with a dup ACK containing the correct sequence number, then drops it.

`wrong-md5` : This adds a fake TCP MD5 signature option and server without MD5 drops it

Here we append a TCP option with kind=19 and length=18 to the TCP header. The kind 19 is the MD5 signature option (RFC 2385), if the receiver doesn't use TCP MD5 (which is basically everything except some BGP routers), it sees an unknown option

issues.title: XHTTP: Add configurable error responses
issues.body:
## What

Adds an optional `errorResponse` object to the XHTTP inbound settings, replacing the bare status-only rejections with a service-consistent appearance.

Currently every rejected request is answered with a bare status code: no body, no `Content-Type` (Go's default "404 page not found" or nothing at all). From the terminating side (CDN, reverse proxy, monitoring) a server that answers *every* unknown path with a naked status code and no content type does not look like a normal service.

- `body` and `contentType` apply to every error response the hub writes (404 unknown path, 400/405/409/413/500 etc.), giving all rejections a uniform, service-consistent appearance.
- `statusCode` overrides the status for requests failing the padding validation — the effective authentication gate — allowing 403 semantics instead of the default 400.
- When `errorResponse` is unset, the behavior is unchanged.

Example:

```json
"xhttpSettings": {
  "path": "/api/v2/stream",
  "errorResponse": {
    "statusCode": 403,
    "body": "{\"error\":\"forbidden\"}",
    "contentType": "application/json"
  }
}
```

Resulting surface: unknown paths → `404 {"error":"forbidden"}`, the API gate without valid padding → `403` with the same body — a coherent API host instead of a bare 404/400 machine.

## Notes

- Server-side only. Round-trips through `extra` like the other settings.
- `config.pb.go` regenerated with protoc v6.33.5 / protoc-gen-go v1.36.11 (matches all existing `.pb.go` headers; unmodified proto regenerates byte-identical with this toolchain).
- Proto field `errorResponse = 31` — merges cleanly alongside #7247 (`responseHeaders = 30`); both features are independent.

## Tests

- `Test_WriteErrorResponse`: bare default when unset, configured body + content type, padding-reject status default (400) and override (403).
- `go test ./...` passes locally across all packages, except the pre-existing network-dependent `TestQUICNameServer` in `app/dns`, which fails identically on pristine `main` in my environment (no QUIC egress).

> How is this different from reverting to the behavior prior to [#7325 ?](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/7325)

Setting no IPv6 DNS in the `dns` list doesn't mean doing nothing for IPv6 DNS; it means clearing it.

So before #7325, on some systems with globally disabled IPv6 or where changing IPv6 settings is prohibited, we encountered an error when setting up the TUN, because Xray tried to clear IPv6 DNS that doesn't exist at all or that we don't have access to.

Now, with this PR, when users don't set IPv6 at all (in `gateway`, `autoSystemRoutingTable` or `dns`), we just ignore the error from clearing the IPv6 DNS. Otherwise we still return the error.

In #7325, we only looked at `gateway` and `autoSystemRoutingTable`, and if they had no IPv6, we ignored the error from setting the IPv6 DNS. The change relative to #7325: now, if users set IPv6 in the `dns` list, we don't ignore the error from setting the IPv6 DNS, even if `gateway` and `autoSystemRoutingTable` have no IPv6.

comments.body:
> @patterniha 更新文档 [XTLS/Xray-docs-next#903](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-docs-next/pull/903)
> 
> 虽然这么改跟 `autoSystemWfpBlockLeak` "misconfigtun" 一样抽象，如果用户那两项都没配置 IPv6，为什么配置 IPv6 `dns`？
> 
> 况且 `gateway` 都没有 IPv6 的话，`dns` 有 IPv6 真的实际有用吗？以及 Windows 上自动分配 `gateway`，这个判断结果可靠吗？
> 
> 再说如果 IPv6 被系统级 disable 了，`gateway` 和 `autoSystemRoutingTable` 含 IPv6 不退出吗？为什么 `dns` 搞特殊？
> 
> ~如果追求即使 IPv6 被系统级 disable 了，那些设置项含 IPv6 也不会阻止 TUN 启动，也不是这么改，虽然可能不该追求这个~

Xray sets the TUN's IPv6 DNS on every start, and just clears it when `dns` has no IPv6 server or isn't set at all. That clearing is what failed for the reporter, so even a TUN with no IPv6 anywhere couldn't start. The check is the same as for the missing IPv6 interface, so it doesn't depend on the addresses Windows assigns.

But you're right that `dns` shouldn't be special: in https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/7332, IPv6 servers in `dns` also keep the TUN from starting, like IPv6 in `gateway` and `autoSystemRoutingTable`. Docs updated in XTLS/Xray-docs-next#903.

comments.issue_title: VLESS protocol: Add lightweight, Post-Quantum ML-KEM-768-based PFS 1-RTT / anti-replay 0-RTT AEAD Encryption
comments.body:
### [中文](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/5067#issue-3361308276) | Русский
> Неофициальный перевод с китайского. При расхождениях с оригиналом приоритет у оригинала.

~~Благодаря [многократным](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4952#issuecomment-3129991254) [слёзным мольбам (написанным кровью)](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4915#issuecomment-3102172861) одного лишь @gfw-killer встроенное шифрование VLESS наконец-то появилось!~~

Я хотел написать эту спецификацию кратко и по существу. Если хотите подробнее узнать о компромиссах, на которые пришлось пойти при проектировании, см. обсуждение, начиная с [этого комментария](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4952#issuecomment-3159885555), а также россыпь вопросов и ответов, начиная с [этого сообщения](https://t.me/projectXtls/1005). Огромное спасибо @Fangliding, @wwqgtxx, @ForestL18, @xchacha20-poly1305 и другим за участие в обсуждении и обратную связь.

## Философия дизайна VLESS Encryption и процесс обмена

Как я говорил ещё год назад: поскольку GFW уже внёс «полностью случайный» внешний вид трафика в чёрный список, **нативный вид шифрования VLESS не является полностью случайным** (в заголовке есть признаки открытого ключа, а трафик несёт признак AEAD-заголовка TLSv1.3 `23 3 3 l>>8 l`, **но можно включить XOR и получить полностью случайный вид**). Главное здесь — **более высокая безопасность, которой нет у SS 2022/AEAD, VMess и других протоколов (прямая секретность и устойчивость к квантовым атакам), и лучшая производительность (при этом рекомендуется включать XTLS, чтобы избежать повторного шифрования и расшифрования), и при этом тот же 0-RTT — чтобы это могла быть более достойная замена, подходящая для сценариев с CDN (чтобы не раскрывать UUID и проксируемый SNI), с промежуточными узлами/ретрансляцией (где запрещены HTTP/TLS), с non-TLS (HTTP в Иране) и т. п.**

Особо отмечу: это шифрование предназначено не для того, чтобы напрямую обходить блокировки. Подобные протоколы давно непригодны для прямого обхода; для этого следует использовать [REALITY](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/pull/4915), [XHTTP](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/discussions/4113), [Vision](https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/discussions/1295) и им подобные.

~~REALITY не требует дополнительного шифрования VLESS, но если вы пользуетесь провайдером-«аэропортом» (платным прокси-сервисом), то можете использовать его линию как промежуточный узел и пересылать трафик на свой бесплатный VPS, обходя аудит со стороны «аэропорта»~~

Как и в замысле шифрования, описанном пять лет назад в VLESS BETA, и в зарезервированной тогда структуре конфигурации, **шифрование VLESS устроено как дополнительный слой conn поверх открытого протокола VLESS и не связано с внутренним протоколом VLESS: его легко реализовать и легко заменить; максимальный размер блока ограничен 8K/16K, что исключает лишнее копирование и не снижает производительность.**

Я написал две версии шифрования, в итоге осталась вторая — она очень лаконична; подробности реализации смотрите в коде, а здесь вкратце опишу процесс обмена:

0. Независимо от того, 1-RTT это или 0-RTT, после каждого установления соединения клиент отправляет ivAndRelays, построенные на нескольких открытых ключах из конфигурации, чтобы обеспечить многократную ретрансляцию до расшифровки.
1. C client hello: длина, зашифрованная nfsKey; открытый ключ MLKEM768X25519 с прямой секретностью, зашифрованный nfsKey; padding, зашифрованный nfsKey.
2. S server hello: открытый ключ MLKEM768X25519 с прямой секретностью, зашифрованный nfsKey; ticket, зашифрованный unitedKey; padding, зашифрованный unitedKey.
3. C ticket hello: длина, зашифрованная nfsKey; ticket, зашифрованный nfsKey; внутренний протокол VLESS, зашифрованный unitedKey.
4. S random hello: 16 случайных байт; внутренний протокол VLESS, зашифрованный unitedKey (везде unitedKey — это согласованные pfsKey плюс nfsKey).
5. **Последующие соединения могут начинаться сразу с шага 3, без 1-RTT-согласовани

comments.issue_title: DefaultListener: do not disable MPTCP

issues.title: macOS: NAT64-synthesized IPv6 endpoint passed to wireguard-go without brackets → IPC error -22, AmneziaWG can't connect (DNS64 networks)
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
On macOS, when an AmneziaWG server is added by **hostname** (A record only, no AAAA) and the Mac is on a network with **DNS64/NAT64** (e.g. mobile hotspot of a Russian mobile operator), the hostname resolves to a NAT64-synthesized address `64:ff9b::/96`. The macOS daemon then passes it to wireguard-go as `endpoint=<ipv6>:<port>` **without square brackets**, wireguard-go rejects it with IPC error -22, peer creation fails and the connection is immediately dropped (the GUI may sit in "Preparing"/"Connecting").

The same server added by **IPv4 literal** works on the same network. Android client works with the hostname on the same network. Same root cause as the Linux issue #2607, but on macOS and triggered by NAT64 synthesis rather than a real AAAA record.

**Root cause (from source, dev @ 7f9b7db)**
`client/platforms/macos/daemon/wireguardutilsmacos.cpp`, `WireguardUtilsMacos::updatePeer()`:
```cpp
if (!config.m_serverIpv4AddrIn.isNull()) {
    out << "endpoint=" << config.m_serverIpv4AddrIn << ":";      // <- holds 64:ff9b::… here, no brackets
} else if (!config.m_serverIpv6AddrIn.isNull()) {
    out << "endpoint=[" << config.m_serverIpv6AddrIn << "]:";
```
The resolved hostname result ends up in `m_serverIpv4AddrIn` even when it is an IPv6 (NAT64) address. Suggested fix: bracket the address whenever it contains `:` (or put IPv6 results into `m_serverIpv6AddrIn`), and/or prefer A records when resolving the endpoint host.

**To Reproduce**
1. Add a self-hosted AmneziaWG server by hostname that has only an A record (e.g. `relay.example.net` → `203.0.113.10`).
2. Connect the Mac to a DNS64/NAT64 network (mobile hotspot).
3. Click Connect → immediately disconnected.

**Service log** (`/private/var/log/AmneziaVPN/AmneziaVPN-service.log`, key/addresses anonymized)
```
MacosRouteMonitor : Adding exclusion route for 64:ff9b::cb00:710a/128
WireguardUtilsMacos : Configuring peer <pubkey> via 64:ff9b::cb00:710a
WireguardGo : ERROR: (utun4) IPC error -22: failed to set endpoint 64:ff9b::cb00:710a:5275: invalid ip:port "64:ff9b::cb00:710a:5275", IPv6 addresses must be surrounded by square brackets
WireguardUtilsMacos : Peer configuration failed: Unknown error: -22
Daemon : Peer creation failed.
DaemonLocalServerConnection : Failed to activate the interface
```

**Expected behavior**
Connection succeeds (bracketed endpoint `[64:ff9b::cb00:710a]:5275`), or the client uses the A record.

**Environment**
- AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 (de93650), macOS Sequoia 15.7.5 (x86_64)
- Protocol: AmneziaWG, self-hosted server added via hostname

issues.title: [iOS][5.1.0.6] AWG 3.1: connected but no traffic — path-update loop rebinds UDP socket every 2–3 s (works in 5.0.3.0 and AmneziaWG)
issues.body:
## Summary

On iOS, AmneziaVPN **5.1.0.6** connects with an AWG 3.1 profile (handshake confirmed) but no traffic passes. The same profile works in AmneziaVPN **5.0.3.0** and in the **AmneziaWG** app on the same phone.

The tunnel log shows a loop: every 2–3 seconds the network extension handles a "network change", re-applies the endpoint config and rebinds the UDP socket. The interface list does not change between these events.

## Environment

| | Fails | Works | Works |
|---|---|---|---|
| App | AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6 (`ac175c8a8`) | AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 | AmneziaWG (App Store) |
| Device / iOS | iPhone, iOS 26.6.2 | iPhone, iOS 27.2 | same iPhone as "Fails", iOS 26.6.2 |
| Network | LTE (Russian mobile carrier) | LTE, same carrier | LTE, same carrier |
| Profile | same AWG 3.1 profile (self-hosted server, MTU 1280) | same | same |

- The server is a self-hosted AmneziaWG 3.1 server (amneziawg-go). The client receives the handshake response. On the server, the peer's transfer stops after ~16 KB.
- In 5.1.0.6, a profile to a server inside the same country works. Only the server abroad fails. This matches the socket rebind loop: each rebind creates a new UDP flow, and new flows to foreign addresses can be filtered on mobile networks. This part is a hypothesis.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On iOS 26.6.2, install AmneziaVPN 5.1.0.6.
2. Import an AWG 3.1 profile (`vpn://`).
3. Connect over LTE.
4. Open any website.

**Expected:** traffic passes, as in 5.0.3.0 and in AmneziaWG.
**Actual:** status is "Connected" and the handshake is confirmed, but no websites load.

## Tunnel log (excerpt, redacted)

```
19:34:14 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - Received handshake response
19:34:16 WG: Observed first handshake at last_handshake_time_sec=...
19:34:18 WG: Network change detected with satisfied route and interface order [pdp_ip0, pdp_ip0, utun8]
19:34:18 WG: Path update state: state=started(...) everHadHandshake=true lastNetworkSettingsUpdateAt=2026-11-04 16:34:14 +0000
19:34:18 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - UAPI: Updating endpoint
19:34:18 WG: UAPI: Updating h1..h4 / s1..s4 padding, header protection key
19:34:18 WG: Routine: receive incoming v4 - stopped
19:34:18 WG: UDP bind has been updated
19:34:18 WG: Routine: receive incoming v4 - started
19:34:18 WG: peer(q6Ht…) - Sending keepalive packet
19:34:21 WG: Network change detected ... [pdp_ip0, pdp_ip0, utun8]   <- same block repeats
19:34:24 ...                                                          <- every 2–3 s
19:34:26 ...
19:34:27 ...
19:34:30 ...
```

`lastNetworkSettingsUpdateAt` does not change, so the app does not re-apply network settings. The path updates come from `NWPathMonitor`. On each update, `WireGuardAdapter.didReceivePathUpdate` (amneziawg-apple v3.1.4) calls `wgSetConfig` and `wgBumpSockets`.

## Analysis

- The two app versions use the same `awg-apple/3.1.4` (see `conanfile.py`). The adapter code is the same.
- One build difference: the `awg-apple` recipe in 5.1.0.6 uses `go/1.27.1` (5.0.3.0 uses `go/1.26.0`).
- The AmneziaWG app on the same phone and iOS version works with the same profile (I did not collect its log). The cause is therefore in the 5.1.0.6 build or the app shell, not in iOS alone.
- I did not find what triggers the repeated path updates in 5.1.0.6.

## Possible fix

In `didReceivePathUpdate`, skip `wgSetConfig` and `wgBumpSockets` when the path has not changed. For example, compare `availableInterfaces` and the status with the last path, and ignore the tunnel's own `utun*` interface.

issues.body:
## Feature request

Please add URL-based import and optional automatic updates for site-based split-tunneling lists, especially on iOS.

This request is about routing lists (domains, IP addresses and CIDR subnets), not subscriptions containing VPN server configurations.

## Use case

I use AmneziaVPN on iOS and want selected destinations to bypass the VPN while all other traffic uses the tunnel.

Currently, distributing and updating an exclusion list requires downloading a JSON file and manually selecting it in the split-tunneling import dialog. If the list changes, each user must repeat this process.

The desired workflow is:

1. A list maintainer publishes a compatible JSON list at a stable HTTPS URL.
2. A user opens an import link (or pastes the HTTPS URL into AmneziaVPN).
3. The app previews the source and routing mode and asks the user to confirm the import.
4. The user can refresh the list manually and optionally enable periodic updates.

This would make it easier to keep the same exclusion list current across devices and share it with family or other users without repeatedly distributing files.

## Proposed behavior

- Import an existing Amnezia site-list JSON file directly from an HTTPS URL.
- Support opening a dedicated deep link or universal link that passes the list URL to AmneziaVPN. The exact link format can be chosen by the maintainers.
- Let the user explicitly select the routing mode. My main use case is "Addresses from the list should not be accessed via VPN"; importing a list should not silently change the existing mode.
- Store the source URL and expose a "Refresh" action, last successful update time, and update errors.
- Offer opt-in automatic refresh, subject to iOS background-execution restrictions; refreshing on app launch or before connection would also be useful.
- Keep downloaded entries associated with their source so that a successful refresh replaces that source's entries, including removals, while preserving independently added local entries.
- Validate the complete response before applying it. On download or validation failure, retain the last successfully imported list.
- Apply updated routes at the next connection if changing them during an active connection is unsupported, and make that behavior clear in the UI.
- Reuse the existing site-list JSON format and supported address types where possible.

A useful first version could support pasting an HTTPS URL and manually refreshing it, with deep links and automatic refresh added later.

## Related work

- #1039 requests additional list formats and automatic downloading/updating of site lists. This request focuses specifically on an HTTPS source, one-link import and its update lifecycle.
- #2449 concerns sharing split-tunneling settings through JSON files.
- #1423 tracks broader improvements to site-based split tunneling.
- PR #2506 proposed server-managed bypass rules and client synchronization, but was closed without merging. Its description explicitly excludes a full subscription/update system for external third-party lists. The workflow requested here would allow a list hosted independently of the VPN server.
- #3298 requests URL subscriptions for VPN server configurations, which is a separate use case.

## Platform

Primary use case: AmneziaVPN on iOS. The same list-source mechanism would also be useful on other platforms.

issues.title: fix(import): accept plain user info in ss:// links
issues.body:
## Summary

`serialization::ss::Deserialize` always base64-decodes the user name of a SIP002 `ss://` link. SIP002 also allows plain, percent-encoded `method:password` user info, and SIP022 requires it for the Shadowsocks 2022 ciphers (`2022-blake3-*`). Such a link, for example `ss://2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm:<key>%3D@host:8388#name`, fails to import with "Can't find the colon separator between method and password".

Closes #3392

## Changes

- `client/core/utils/serialization/ss.cpp`: when the user info has a password part, the method and password come from the decoded user name and password. Links with base64 user info take the same path as before.
- `client/tests/testShadowSocksSerialization.cpp`: new Qt Test that covers a base64 link and a plain SS-2022 link (method, password, address, port).
- `client/tests/CMakeLists.txt`: registers `test_shadowsocks_serialization` as `ShadowSocksSerializationTest`.

## Testing

The new test against the parser sources (`ss.cpp`, `outbound.cpp`, `inbound.cpp`, `utilities.cpp`), built with Qt 6.8.2 on Debian 13 x86_64:

- Without the fix: `Totals: 3 passed, 1 failed` (`plain user info` fails with the error above).
- With the fix: `Totals: 4 passed, 0 failed`.

I didn't run the full app build (Qt 6.10 and Conan) or `ctest` locally, so CI covers the new CMake target. The touched lines follow `.clang-format`.

issues.title: Shadowsocks 2022 ss:// links fail to import: "Can't find the colon separator between method and password"
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
Importing a SIP002 `ss://` link whose user info is plain `method:password` instead of base64 fails. SIP022 requires this form for the Shadowsocks 2022 ciphers (`2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm`, `2022-blake3-aes-256-gcm`, `2022-blake3-chacha20-poly1305`), so these links cannot be imported at all.

`serialization::ss::Deserialize` (`client/core/utils/serialization/ss.cpp`) always passes the URL user name through `Utils::SafeBase64Decode`. For a plain link the user name is the method alone, so the decoded text has no colon and the parser returns an empty config.

**To Reproduce**
1. Copy a link of the form `ss://2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm:dGVzdC1rZXktMDEyMzQ1Njc4OWFiY2RlZg%3D%3D@ss.example.com:8388#test`.
2. Import it from the clipboard or the "Insert key" field.
3. The import fails. `ss::Deserialize` reports "Can't find the colon separator between method and password".

**Expected behavior**
The link imports with method `2022-blake3-aes-128-gcm` and password `dGVzdC1rZXktMDEyMzQ1Njc4OWFiY2RlZg==`, as it already does when the same user info is base64-encoded.

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: any (shared import code)
 - Version: current `dev` (ac175c8)

**Additional context**
SIP002: https://shadowsocks.org/doc/sip002.html. SIP022: https://shadowsocks.org/doc/sip022.html. Xray-core supports the 2022 ciphers.

issues.title: [Windows][XRay] Client blackholes traffic to private DNS address (AmneziaDNS unreachable), ignores DNS settings from sharing config, leaves stale KillSwitch DNS filters after toggling
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows, the XRay connection shows "Connected" and TCP transport through the tunnel works perfectly, but the client never delivers packets destined to the private AmneziaDNS address (172.29.172.254) into the tunnel — they are accepted by the local xray and blackholed on the laptop (confirmed by packet captures on both ends). Since KillSwitch forbids any other DNS, hostname resolution is impossible: "connected but no websites open". iOS client against the same server uses AmneziaDNS flawlessly.

Two additional independent problems found while diagnosing:
1. Client DNS settings are ignored in favor of DNS information embedded in the sharing config.
2. The tunnel adapter's DNS assignment and the KillSwitch/WFP DNS allow-list are driven by different logic, can contradict each other, and stale WFP filters persist until a Windows reboot.

Full layered diagnosis below (following the A/B/C/D framework proposed in #3148). Same user-facing symptom as #1345 (closed unresolved). Unlike the case discussed in #3148, the server-side path here is proven healthy.

### To Reproduce

1. Deploy XRay (XHTTP + REALITY) + AmneziaDNS on a self-hosted server from an iOS client (5.0.2.1 in my case)
2. Share the connection config to a Windows 11 machine, connect with XRay
3. Try to open any website → nothing resolves; `nslookup wikipedia.org` times out through all retries
4. `nslookup -vc` (TCP) to 172.29.172.254 hangs as well; apps with hardcoded IPs (Telegram) keep working
5. `curl -v --resolve www.wikipedia.org:443:185.15.59.224 https://www.wikipedia.org/` → 200 OK, full page — TCP transport is healthy, only DNS is dead

### Expected behavior

- DNS queries to the AmneziaDNS address should be routed into the tunnel like any other tunnel-bound traffic (iOS does this correctly against the same server).
- Client DNS settings should take precedence over (or at least not be silently overridden by) DNS information embedded in a sharing config.
- The tunnel adapter's DNS assignment and the KillSwitch DNS allow-list should always agree, and all WFP filters should be removed on disconnect.

### Log files

Attached: app + service logs from a failing session (secrets redacted: server IP → SERVER_IP, socks5 credentials → REDACTED). issues.title: [Linux][5.0.3.0] Error 101: sudo stalls during hostname resolution in IPv6 setup
issues.body:
## Environment

- OS: Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS (x86_64), COSMIC desktop
- Client: AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 (`de93650`)
- VPN protocol: Xray
- Connection imported via **Share connection** from phone
- Service: `AmneziaVPN.service` running as root; `ExecStart=/opt/AmneziaVPN/bin/AmneziaVPN-service`

## Description

On Linux, attempting to connect ends with `ErrorCode::101 (Internal Error)`. Xray and `tun2socks` start, but the client fails at the step where it tries to disable IPv6 routing:

```text
Failed to disable IPv6 routing
Could not disable ipv6
QProcess: Destroyed while process ("sudo") is still running.
```

In this case the underlying cause was a blocking hostname-resolution call from `sudo`, not an inability of the Linux kernel to change the IPv6 setting.

## Reproduction and evidence

The computer hostname was `Vector`, but `/etc/hosts` did **not** initially contain an entry for that hostname:

```text
127.0.0.1 localhost
::1 localhost
```

`/etc/nsswitch.conf` used:

```text
hosts: files mdns4_minimal [NOTFOUND=return] resolve [!UNAVAIL=return] dns myhostname
```

A trace of the Amnezia service and its children showed the following sequence (trimmed for clarity):

```text
14:06:38.406468 execve("/usr/bin/sudo", ["/usr/bin/sudo", "sysctl", "-w", "net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1"], ...)
...
connect(6, {sa_family=AF_UNIX, sun_path="/run/systemd/resolve/io.systemd.Resolve"}, 42) = 0
sendto(6, "{\"method\":\"io.systemd.Resolve.ResolveHostname\",\"parameters\":{\"name\":\"Vector\",\"flags\":0}}\\0", ...) = 89
recvfrom(6, ..., MSG_DONTWAIT, ...) = -1 EAGAIN
ppoll([{fd=6, events=POLLIN}], 1, {tv_sec=119, ...}, NULL, 8 <unfinished ...>
14:06:40.418560 kill(87730, SIGKILL) = 0
...
+++ killed by SIGKILL +++
```

A second trace reproduced the same pattern, again showing `sudo` waiting for a reply from `systemd-resolved` and being killed about 2 seconds later.

Other findings:

- `/dev/net/tun` was present and usable.
- The Amnezia systemd service ran as root; `PATH` included `/usr/bin` and `/usr/sbin`.
- IPv6 was enabled at kernel level (`net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=0`).
- Manually setting `net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6=1` and `net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=1`, then restoring both to `0`, completed within approximately 1–6 ms.
- The equivalent privileged writes via `sudo` in a temporary systemd service also completed in approximately 5–6 ms.
- A service restart alone did not resolve the original connection failure.

## Confirmed workaround

Adding a local hostname mapping and restarting the service:

```text
127.0.1.1 Vector
```

```bash
sudo systemctl restart AmneziaVPN.service
```

After this, the client successfully established the VPN connection and stopped reporting Error 101.

## Expected behavior

The client should handle hostname-resolution/subprocess failures gracefully and display a precise diagnostic rather than a generic IPv6 error. Since the service already runs as root, consider whether calling `sudo` is necessary. At minimum, the failure should identify a subprocess timeout or local hostname-resolution issue.

## Related, separate problem

After connection succeeded, a shared-Xray-config DNS issue remained; it was fixed by reissuing the share link with AmneziaDNS disabled and is being documented separately in #3198.

comments.issue_title: [Windows][XRay] Client blackholes traffic to private DNS address (AmneziaDNS unreachable), ignores DNS settings from sharing config, leaves stale KillSwitch DNS filters after toggling
comments.body:
I can confirm a very similar **shared-config DNS failure on Linux**, specifically **Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS (COSMIC), AmneziaVPN 5.0.3.0 (`de93650`), Xray**.

The VPN connection was originally created on a phone and then imported to the Linux laptop using **Share connection**. It displayed **Connected**, and HTTPS through the tunnel worked when bypassing DNS (`curl --resolve` returned `HTTP/2 200`), but ordinary DNS requests timed out and websites would not load.

Diagnostics:

- `resolvectl status tun2` showed `172.29.172.254` as the resolver despite setting `1.1.1.1` and `1.0.0.1` in the client.
- `resolvectl query -4 example.com` timed out.
- Local Xray repeatedly logged `accepted udp:172.29.172.254:53` (and also TCP/53), with no DNS response observed.
- The Amnezia firewall's `amnvpn.320.allowDNS` ACCEPT counters increased on `tun2` during lookups (UDP/53: 14 -> 34 packets; TCP/53: 0 -> 32), while `amnvpn.310.blockDNS` and `amnvpn.100.blockAll` counters remained at 0. That shows DNS requests were allowed by those local rules, not where the replies were lost.
- With VPN disconnected, `resolvectl query example.com` succeeded in ~31 ms.

**Confirmed fix:** On the phone, I **disabled AmneziaDNS, generated a new sharing link, and imported that new configuration into Linux**. This immediately fixed the DNS issue. The new `resolvectl status tun2` showed:

```text
Current DNS Server: 1.0.0.1
DNS Servers: 1.1.1.1 1.0.0.1
DNS Domain: ~.
```

`resolvectl query -4 example.com` succeeded in ~290 ms, and a normal `curl -4 -I --noproxy '*' https://example.com` returned `HTTP/2 200`.

This suggests that the issue with DNS information embedded in a shared Xray configuration / client DNS handling also affects **Linux**, not only Windows. The exact point where traffic to the private DNS destination is lost was **not conclusively proven** in my Linux test.
